body:
You are drafting short lines of game text for a single-player D&D 2024 computer RPG set in Curse of Strahd's Barovia. Reply in plain text only. Do not message, route to, or ask anyone else; finish with your reply.

HOUSE RULES FOR ALL LINES
- ALLUDE, NEVER QUOTE. This game winks at another famous fantasy game in small ways, but no line may contain a name, quote, or catchphrase from another game, and no line may mention a game, a player, dice, rolls, levels or saving. Everything happens inside the world.
- The tone is gothic, dry and quietly funny, never cruel. The joke is in what is there.
- Give TWO options for every line so the editor can choose. Label each option A or B.
- Spoken lines are formatted: Speaker [mood]: Text   (mood optional: neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly, weary). One or two sentences a line.

THE NARRATOR (voice rules): an old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather: interested, no illusions. Second person, present tense ("You crouch..."), or the acting hero as {name}. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn. Concrete senses, not adjectives. Never tells the player what to feel. No modern slang. When an animal speaks through the Speak with Animals spell, the Narrator reports it in quotes, in plain animal pictures (a dog says "the digger-man", "the box-maker").

THE PLACE: the study of an old, famous monster hunter's tower on a lake. Real line: "Jars and bottles in neat rows, each labelled in a small hand: wolfsbane, garlic oil, grave dirt (three cemeteries), holy water (blessed twice), and one simply marked DO NOT."
THE JAR: the one marked DO NOT holds, in cloudy spirit, a small grey thing with feelers, about the length of a finger. The hunter's label on the back, in his small precise hand, says it was taken from the eye of a sailor (or a stranger) in a far country, a man who swore a ship shaped like a squid had fallen out of the sky with him aboard; that the thing turns to face whoever looks at it; and that it must not be opened. The player heard about that man in a village tavern long ago (a man who walked east with a worm in his eye).
Words NOT to use: tadpole, illithid, mind flayer, nautiloid.

WRITE:
1. NARRATOR, the close look at the jar SUCCEEDS (Arcana): the thing in the spirit, and it turning toward the looker. One or two sentences, under 40 words. Use {name}.
2. NARRATOR, the look FAILS: the spirit is too cloudy; something in it might have moved. One sentence, under 25 words.
3. THE LABEL (journal text, 50 to 80 words) in the hunter's small precise hand: where and from whom, the squid-shaped ship, that it faces the looker, DO NOT OPEN. Never names the hunter or the sailor.

Return exactly this layout:
1A: Narrator: ...
1B: Narrator: ...
2A: Narrator: ...
2B: Narrator: ...
3A: ...
3B: ...
result:
1A: Narrator: Suspended in the yellowed spirit hangs a finger-length of grey flesh with four pale feelers at the snout. As {name} leans close, the pickled thing turns slowly in the jar to face {name}'s eye.
1B: Narrator: Through the cloudy brine, {name} makes out a grey, finger-long creature curled upon itself like a peeled grub. Its blind end lifts, feelers parting, and swivels through the spirit until it points straight at {name}.
2A: Narrator: The spirit in the jar is clouded thick as tallow, though a grey shape inside shifts—or settles—as your shadow crosses the glass.
2B: Narrator: Nothing shows through the murky brine save a pale smudge the length of a finger, which may only have drifted when the floorboards creaked.
3A: Extracted with silver forceps from the left eye of a shipwrecked sailor in a western port. The man swore a vessel shaped like a squid had fallen burning from the sky with him aboard. Though kept five winters in strong spirit, the specimen is not dead; it turns in the jar to face whoever looks upon it. DO NOT OPEN.
3B: Taken in a far country from behind the eye of a wandering stranger who walked east in a fever. He claimed a great ship with the arms of a squid had dropped out of the heavens and broken upon the hills. Even pickled in spirit, the grey thing pivots by its feelers to watch whichever face approaches the glass. Keep the wax sealed. DO NOT OPEN.
